negative_findings.description: Direct WebFetch of https://www.nbrm.mk/registar-na-institucii-za-elektronski-pari.nspx returned HTTP 403 Forbidden. The page is indexed by search engines and other nbrm.mk pages are widely referenced, so this is almost certainly bot protection rather than a dead page.
negative_findings.result_summary: Could not read the authoritative EMI register contents; the licensed-entity list had to be reconstructed indirectly from press reports (Paysera Македонија, Iute Pay).
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The register is the single authoritative roster for this cell; without it the actor map is press-derived and may be incomplete or stale.

negative_findings.description: No separate, publicly visible NBRSM register page for payment institutions (as distinct from e-money institutions) or for payment-system operators was surfaced by either mk or en searches, although the licensing decision on registers implies all three exist.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only the EMI register URL was recovered; the PI and operator register URLs remain unknown.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Payment institutions (not EMIs) are likely the larger population — remittance and acquiring-adjacent actors — so the actor map has a structural hole.

negative_findings.description: No dedicated MK register or supervised list of crypto-asset service providers / crypto exchanges was found; local reporting describes crypto exchanges as operating legally but without a licensing regime.
negative_findings.result_summary: Crypto-adjacent payment apps in MK cannot currently be enumerated from any official register.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The crypto-adjacent portion of this cell must be tracked through company sites and press only, with low completeness confidence.

negative_findings.description: Searches did not surface a Ria Money Transfer MK country/agent page or an official Pošta na Severna Makedonija remittance-payout page, even though Ria is named among the channels operating in MK.
negative_findings.result_summary: Ria's and the postal network's MK distribution footprint is undocumented in what I found.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Postal and Ria networks are typically material rural cash-out channels; missing them understates the non-bank payout footprint.

negative_findings.description: The Paysera Македонија corporate URL (paysera.mk) is my inference from the entity name, not a URL I observed in results; only the IT.mk article about its e-money approval was actually surfaced.
negative_findings.result_summary: Candidate recorded with low confidence and an explicit verification instruction.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Recording an inferred URL as if observed would violate the no-fabrication rule; the downstream verification pass must resolve it.

coverage_gaps.description: The full licensed population of payment institutions, e-money institutions and payment-system operators in MK is not enumerated — only two EMIs (Paysera Македонија, Iute Pay) are known by name from press.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Retrieve the NBRSM registers with a browser-grade fetcher (real UA, cookies, JS) or via a formal information request; index all three registers and diff monthly.

coverage_gaps.description: Non-bank exchange offices (менувачници) and financial companies (финансиски друштва) that act as remittance and cash-handling nodes were only partially covered — UFS was found, but no register of exchange offices or financial companies was located.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Search the Ministry of Finance / NBRSM lists of овластени менувачи and финансиски друштва, and the Central Registry (crm.com.mk) by activity code, to build the full cash-in/cash-out node inventory.

coverage_gaps.description: No source found that separates non-bank PSP/EMI transaction volumes from bank-channel volumes; NBRSM card/e-commerce statistics and AETM analyses appear to report the aggregate.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Inspect the NBRSM payment-statistics tables at row level once accessible to check for a PI/EMI breakout; if absent, model the split from operator disclosures (Iute Group reports) and note it as an estimate.

coverage_gaps.description: Agent/branch-level geographic footprint of cash-out points (WU/MoneyGram/Ria agents, UFS agencies, bank branches) is not consolidated anywhere found.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build a geocoded dataset by scraping each operator's locator (UFS, Halkbank, WU global locator) quarterly; this becomes proprietary intelligence no public source offers.

coverage_gaps.description: Albanian-language sources were not searched, although a large share of MK remittance-receiving households are Albanian-speaking and some agent networks and fintech marketing are Albanian-language.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add an Albanian (sq) query pass — e.g. 'institucion pagesash', 'para elektronike', 'transferta parash', 'remitanca' — targeting MK-domain and Tetovo/Gostivar-area sources.

brief: North Macedonia's non-bank payments landscape became legible only recently: the PSD2/EMD2-transposing Law on Payment Services and Payment Systems (in force 2023) created payment-institution and e-money-institution licences, and the first grants landed in 2025 (Paysera Македонија as the first domestic EMI, Iute Pay shortly after). The authoritative sources are NBRSM's public registers, card/ATM/POS statistics and crypto guidance — all on a bot-defended host that returned 403 to automated fetching and will need browser-grade collection. Around the regulator sit three high-value non-official layers: infrastructure operators (CaSys as the sole domestic processor with the cPay gateway; Monri/Payten regionally), the remittance distribution layer (UFS with a reported 250+ non-bank Western Union agencies, plus bank agent pages for WU/MoneyGram/Ria that disclose payout points and tariffs), and a strong intermediary-analytics layer (AETM/ecommerce.mk quarterly online-transaction values, IT.mk and Bankarstvo.mk for entrant news). The main blind spots are the un-enumerated PI register, the absence of any crypto-service-provider register, and no public split of non-bank versus bank transaction volumes.
